newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex sells new gasoline for high-end Mexican cars.
newsitem.headline: Pemex sells new gasoline for high-end Mexican cars.

text.p: A new gasoline in Mexico City will help the city's classier cars run more efficiently but may not make a dent in perennial pollution problems, environmentalists said Wednesday.
State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) recently unveiled the higher-octane unleaded gasoline, called Pemex Premium.
Motorists pay a 10 percent more for the gasoline, which sells for about 3.2 pesos per liter compared with 2.9 pesos per liter for Pemex Magna, Mexico's regular unleaded gasoline.

"The gasoline will benefit high performance autos like the Mercedes Benz, BMW or the more luxurious Nissans. It will only be sold in some gasoline stations in the neighborhoods where people can afford these types of cars," Carlos Sandoval, head of the Industrial Ecologists Council, told Reuters.
When tested in the northern industrial center Monterrey, the Premium gasoline was not widely used, he said.

Premium has the same characteristics as reformulated unleaded gasoline, but has an octane level of 92, five points higher than standard unleaded here. High octane gas burns fuel more efficiently, using less gas.

"The country's liberation of trade has allowed the introduction of new models and brands of high performance cars, meaning highly efficient motors that...use higher octane unleaded gasoline," Pemex said in a statement.

Authorities hope the Premium and reformulated unleaded gasolines, unveiled just two months ago, will reduce hydrocarbon emissions in Mexico City by 12 percent for cars with catalytic converters, Pemex's Mexican Petroleum Institute said.
Meanwhile, environmentalists stopped short of endorsing the gasoline, saying they are waiting to complete further studies on the environmental impact.
Mexico City's metropolitan area still has about 1.8 million cars out of a total of three million that lack catalytic converters.
Environmentalists say these older cars are the number-one cause of Mexico City's smog, which is among the worst in the world.

Cars without catalytic converters emit three times the amount of nitrogen, up to six times the amount of hydrocarbons and 16 times the amount of carbon monoxide as cars with catalytic converters, Pemex said.
